title: VPC Quarantine & Offline Upgrade Acceptance Checklist
creator: Aisha Chen
description: This ticket consolidates requirements and measurable acceptance criteria for performing operator-driven upgrades in isolated VPCs and air-gapped sites. Focus is on a quarantine-first upgrade flow that limits egress, verifies artifacts locally, and provides deterministic rollback triggers. This PRD is scoped to the operator/controller behaviors, networking prechecks (DNS, MTU, split-horizon), and the offline artifact verification choreography; infra work for mirror provisioning and UI rollout controls will be tracked by linked engineering tickets.
requirements: Quarantine mode: cluster can be placed into a quarantine state that blocks all non-whitelisted egress during upgrade windows
Artifact verification: operator must validate signed artifact checksums locally against an operator-managed trust store before applying images
Mirror bootstrap: operator supports staged pull from a local mirror (HTTP or filesystem) with configurable bandwidth caps
Split-horizon DNS: operator must optionally use a customer-provided split-horizon DNS mapping for internal registry endpoints
Canary scope: support node- and rack-scoped canary, with configurable success thresholds and max-failure counts
Rollback automation: operator will automatically rollback on health-check regression or failed post-upgrade preflight within a configurable timeout
KMS rotation sanity: verify KMS/HSM connectivity or local key fallback for secret re-encryption post-upgrade
Operator idempotency: repeated upgrade attempts must be idempotent and safe to retry after partial failure
Minimal operator privileges: the upgrade flow must be achievable without granting external egress to control-plane nodes beyond whitelisted mirror/registry endpoints
Observability hooks: emit structured events for each phase (prepare, fetch, verify, stage, commit, post-verify, rollback) to customer logs
acceptance_criteria: Network prechecks pass: validation script verifies cluster IP routing, MTU >= configured value, and split-horizon DNS resolves registry hostnames to mirror addresses; failure blocks upgrade

Offline verification success: for test clusters, operator should fetch artifacts from local mirror and validate signatures using the provided trust anchor; logs must show signature verification result
Quarantine enforcement: during quarantine mode, any outbound connection attempt to non-whitelisted hosts is dropped and logged; test harness validates 100% deny for non-whitelisted egress
Staged canary rollout: canary of 5% of nodes succeeds with <1% tokenization errors and service latency within 2x baseline before proceeding to remainder
Automated rollback trigger: simulate a failing post-upgrade probe (e.g., KV cache mismatch); operator must abort and roll back within configurable timeout and mark run as failed
Bandwidth-throttled mirror pull: large artifact pull from local mirror respects configured throttle within +/-10% of target throughput
KMS fallback: if external KMS is unreachable during post-upgrade key operations, operator must operate in read-only with explicit audit event and fail-safe state rather than exposing plaintext keys
Audit trail: every upgrade run produces an immutable audit entry with artifacts used, checksums, operator user, start/end timestamps, and outcome
Recovery play: documented manual recovery steps (operator override, forced rollback, manual artifact replace) validated by runbook walkthrough
Security review: security_signoff label present and security_review_required == true prior to GA rollout
decision_log: 2025-02-12: Chose quarantine-first pattern (vs. allowing limited egress) to minimize blast radius for regulated customers
2025-02-18: Agreed to require artifact signatures and a trust anchor preconfigured by customer; vendor-signed registry only allowed if customer opts-in
2025-02-22: Scoped canary to node/rack levels; decided not to implement pod-level random sampling for first pass
2025-02-28: Selected operator-driven automatic rollback (timeboxed) rather than human-in-the-loop stop for primary path
2025-03-03: Added KMS fallback requirement after red-team raised concerns about upgrades causing KMS transient failures
risks: Customer mirror misconfiguration causes upgrade to stall; mitigated by preflight mirror health check and clear error messages
Split-horizon DNS complexity may vary by customer environments and cause silent artifact mismatches; mitigated by checksum verification and explicit DNS validation step
Bandwidth-constrained sites may exceed maintenance windows if mirror throttling is mis-set; mitigated by estimated artifact sizes in release notes and adjustable throttle settings
False-positive rollback triggers could increase churn; mitigated with conservative default thresholds and operator-initiated rollback override with audit
test_plan: Automated preflight suite: validate DNS resolution, MTU, mirror health, trust anchor presence
Chaos test: simulate intermittent mirror connectivity during fetch phase and verify idempotent retries
Rollback simulation: run upgrade where post-upgrade liveness probe fails and assert rollback completes cleanly
Air-gap integration test: end-to-end install+upgrade using physical media mirror in isolated testbed
Performance validation: compare critical request p95 latency pre/post upgrade in canary nodes
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal staging): run on RH staging clusters with synthetic traffic and telemetry enabled
Phase 1 (pilot customers): offer to two SOC2 customers in EU with operator assistance; schedule 2 maintenance windows each
Phase 2 (wider beta): enable self-serve quarantine upgrade in Console with enhanced warnings
Phase 3 (GA): enable by default for dedicated/private deployments with security signoff and runbooks attached
